metadata.case_name: WONG WAN CHOW v. SECRETARY FOR JUSTICE FOR AND ON BEHALF OF THE COMMISSIONER FOR LABOUR OF THE HONG KONG SPECIAL ADMINISTRATIVE REGION

plaintiff.occupation_before: newspaper delivery worker (prior to late June/early July 2006)

source: The plaintiff was diagnosed by the Clinic to be suffering from plantar fasciitis which was considered to be a work-related disease.
During all this time her condition of bilateral plantar fasciitis persisted and her pain did not go away.

source: the plaintiff was admitted to the Prince of Wales Hospital and the Shatin Hospital from 2 February 2008 to 23 February 2008 for chronic rheumatic heart disease.
It is undisputed that the plaintiff suffered from chronic rheumatic heart disease
the plaintiff was admitted to the Prince of Wales Hospital and the Shatin Hospital from 2 February 2008 to 23 February 2008 for chronic rheumatic heart disease.
the plaintiff had required in-patient care since 2 February 2008 for her congestive heart failure caused by rheumatic heart disease
congestive heart failure, atrial fibrillation with chronic rheumatic heart disease
the psychiatric report of the plaintiff reveals that the plaintiff suffers from delusional disorder

manifestations.description: persistent bilateral plantar heel pain (pain did not go away)
severe heel pain (reported at times, e.g. 15 January 2008 and November 2007 after work)
inability to resume previous work (unable to continue as newspaper delivery worker)
psychiatric symptoms / delusional disorder (psychiatric condition revealed in report)

treatments_received: health education and counseling (use of ice pads, muscle exercises, wearing of support shoes, weight reduction and avoidance of heavy lifting)
referral to Prosthetic and Orthotics Department (P & O Department) for heel pads
referral to Orthopaedics & Traumatology Department of North District Hospital (referred 13 August 2008)
hospital admission for chronic rheumatic heart disease (2 February 2008 to 23 February 2008)

losses.description: Pain, suffering and loss of amenities due to prolonged bilateral plantar fasciitis; plaintiff's painful condition had been prolonged (judicial assessment, assuming liability).
Inability to resume previous work as a newspaper delivery worker; loss of pre-trial earnings claimed based on $6,000 per month.
